text:
maria: customer reports intermittent JSON-mode parse failures for invoice API. They get HTTP 200 but our client-side strict JSON validation fails: 'invalid JSON: unexpected end of input' on parse step. Happening ~1-2% of requests.
alex: thanks, can you paste the raw response body and their client error? also which model / streaming vs non-streaming?
maria: model=redwood-text-1, using streaming=true. customer sends prompt -> we stream tokens, they reassemble and then fail to parse. sample raw response (reconstructed by customer):

{"invoice_id": 123456, "status": PENDING, "total": "49.99", "paid": null,}

(note trailing comma, status not quoted)
sam: interesting — that body is invalid JSON for multiple reasons: status unquoted (enum casing), trailing comma, invoice_id numeric vs string. but why would streaming produce that sometimes?
leo: could be stream truncation or a partial chunk that gets stitched before final token. check if client closed stream early or our stream sent FIN mid-object. can you share request ids/trace ids?
maria: attaching customer trace ids: RID=rid_3h9X, request_ts=1768004989. customer says ~30% of failures happen right after auth rotation we did yesterday.
support-bot: Created support ticket #SUP-4321 for RID rid_3h9X and linked customer logs.
chris: @eng-runtime can you look at streaming edge case during token refresh? maybe a race when auth cookies rotate and we return a short response with status code 200 but truncated payload.
eng-runtime (via deploy-bot): deploy 2026-03-15 03:12 had new keepalive handling. rolling back to prior keepalive fixed an unrelated timeout last week. I'll correlate.
maria: repro steps from customer (minimal):
1) curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"gen invoice json"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=true 
2) reassemble chunks exactly as received and attempt JSON.parse -> sometimes fails.

Example invalid concat we got:

{"invoice_id":0,"status":PENDING,"total":"null",

then stream closes.

They also see bool/null flips: sometimes "paid": null -> becomes "paid": "null" (string) in other runs.
leo: two hypotheses: 1) stream truncation/clipped chunk causing trailing comma/unquoted token; 2) middleware that canonicalizes nulls/strings during auth proxying when token format changes. check gateway transforms.
sam: I grabbed the backend logs for rid_3h9X: 

[1768004989] INFO request start rid_3h9X stream=true
[1768004991] DEBUG emit chunk "{\"invoice_id\":0,\"status\":PEN"
[1768004991] ERROR connection reset by peer while streaming rid_3h9X
[1768004992] INFO request end rid_3h9X status=200 bytes=102

notice: connection reset but request ended with 200 and bytes=102.
alex: that matches a scenario where a soft error after streaming completion still returns 200 and partial body. Need to see our flush/finalization path.
chris: escalation decision: route to eng-runtime and eng-platform. severity=high because customer invoice parsing failing triggers billing confusion. also cc legal/ops if scope expands.
maria: customer says billing systems silently drop invoices when parse fails. they want a hotfix or a recommended client workaround.
leo: short-term workaround: disable strict JSON on client or implement tolerant parsing that strips trailing commas and unquoted enums; or request non-streaming (stream=false) which sends complete payloads. both are suboptimal.
alex: long term: fix stream-to-200-on-reset -> ensure we return 5xx on truncated payloads or mark response partial in header. also add server-side validation that final token completes object before sending final 200.
maria: I'll scope a reproducible test and attach a minimal harness to the SUP ticket. customer willing to run a test against a staging endpoint.

Next steps agreed:
- eng-runtime to reproduce with auth rotation and connection reset (chris, leo)
- eng-platform to audit gateway transforms during auth rotation (sam)
- support to provide harness + customer traces (maria)
- temporary guidance to customer: use stream=false or tolerant parse + retry (alex)

maria: thanks all, customer will stand by for staging test. :thumbsup:
